note: Option order printed in source = authoring layout only. Runtime MUST shuffle per session and store the permutation.
rules: diagnostic (D) weight 0 — never in Writing level

tasks.label: Functional message
tasks.prompt: Your friend asks: "What time can we meet tomorrow?" Write a reply with a time and place.

tasks.label: Information transfer
tasks.prompt: A notice says: "Library open Monday-Friday 9:00-18:00; Saturday 10:00-14:00; Sunday closed." Write two simple sentences telling a friend when the library is open.

tasks.label: Personal description
tasks.prompt: Write a short message about your usual week. Say where you work or study, one day you are busy, and one thing you enjoy.

tasks.label: Integrated accuracy diagnostic
tasks.prompt: Listen and write: "The bus is late today." This task is diagnostic only and is not part of the Writing CEFR estimate.

tasks.label: Functional email
tasks.prompt: You booked a class for Tuesday but cannot attend. Write to the centre, explain the problem and ask about another day.

tasks.label: Mediation / summary
tasks.prompt: Your friend sends: "The swimming pool is closed on Monday for repairs. It will reopen Tuesday at 10:00. Evening classes are not affected." Write a short message telling another friend the important information.

tasks.label: Advice
tasks.prompt: A friend wants to improve English but has only 30 minutes a day. Give two practical suggestions and explain briefly why they may help.

tasks.label: Integrated accuracy diagnostic
tasks.prompt: Listen and write: "The meeting starts at half past ten." Diagnostic only; excluded from the Writing CEFR estimate.
tasks.audio_script: The meeting starts at half past ten.

tasks.label: Complaint email
tasks.prompt: Your online order arrived two days late and one item is missing. Write to customer service, explain the problem and say what you would like them to do.

tasks.label: Mediation / summary
tasks.prompt: Message A says the morning workshop is full. Message B says the afternoon workshop covers the same material and still has places. Write a short update for a colleague who wanted to attend.

tasks.label: Viewpoint
tasks.prompt: Some people learn better alone, while others learn better in a group. Give your view, two reasons and an example.

tasks.label: Integrated accuracy diagnostic
tasks.prompt: Listen and write: "The workshop was cancelled because the trainer was ill." Diagnostic only.
tasks.audio_script: The workshop was cancelled because the trainer was ill.

tasks.label: Professional email
tasks.prompt: A weekly team meeting often runs over time because updates are too detailed. Write an email proposing a change to the format, explaining the problem, your proposal and one benefit.

tasks.label: Mediation / synthesis
tasks.prompt: Two colleagues disagree about training. One wants a single full-day session; the other prefers three shorter sessions because of staffing. Write a neutral summary of both views and propose one compromise.

tasks.label: Reasoned response
tasks.prompt: Should organisations allow staff to choose where they work, or should they set the same office policy for everyone? Discuss both sides and give a reasoned conclusion.

tasks.label: Integrated accuracy diagnostic
tasks.prompt: Listen and write: "The survey suggests an improvement, but the sample was smaller than expected." Diagnostic only.
tasks.audio_script: The survey suggests an improvement, but the sample was smaller than expected.

tasks.label: Professional correction
tasks.prompt: A project summary says a new process "clearly improved satisfaction", but only a small voluntary group responded. Write to the project lead suggesting more accurate wording and one way to strengthen future evidence.

tasks.label: Mediation / evaluate
tasks.prompt: You receive two short comments about a new public information page. Comment A says it is clearer and faster to use. Comment B says important detail is now harder to find. Write a concise summary that represents both views and recommends a next step.

tasks.label: Evaluation
tasks.prompt: When a decision affects the public, how much uncertainty should an organisation communicate? Develop a balanced argument and give examples.

tasks.label: Integrated accuracy diagnostic
tasks.prompt: Listen and write: "The apparent improvement should be interpreted cautiously because the sample changed." Diagnostic only.
tasks.audio_script: The apparent improvement should be interpreted cautiously because the sample changed.

tasks.label: Executive note
tasks.prompt: A senior executive wants to announce that a pilot was "a clear success". You know one outcome improved strongly, another was unchanged, and participation was low. Draft a concise note recommending accurate public wording.

tasks.label: Cross-text synthesis
tasks.prompt: Two commentaries disagree about whether frequent everyday usage should quickly influence dictionary definitions. Summarise the common ground and the precise disagreement without taking a side.

tasks.label: Critical evaluation
tasks.prompt: Evaluate the proposition: "A transparent decision is one in which all relevant information is made available." Consider selection, information overload, uncertainty and meaningful understanding.

tasks.label: Integrated accuracy diagnostic
tasks.prompt: Listen and write: "A precise estimate can still mislead if the uncertainty around it is hidden." Diagnostic only.
tasks.audio_script: A precise estimate can still mislead if the uncertainty around it is hidden.
